nodes.name: Data Engineering Foundations and Lifecycle
core_concepts: Lifecycle of data creation and usage
Data generation, storage, ingestion, serving, and analytics

assessment_rubric.diagnostic_question: Explain the major stages of the data engineering lifecycle and identify where a data pipeline should enforce quality checks and operational monitoring.
assessment_rubric.socratic_prompt: Why does a system that collects data efficiently but does not store or serve it reliably fail to create business value?
key_evaluation_criteria: Understands the data lifecycle end to end
Links data movement to operational quality
Recognizes that engineering value comes from reliable delivery as well as collection
assessment_rubric.remediation_hint: Map each data object to its producer, storage destination, consumer, and operational controls before optimizing any single stage.

nodes.name: Programming, Linux, and Distributed Systems Basics
core_concepts: Python, Java, Scala, or Go fundamentals

assessment_rubric.diagnostic_question: Describe how you would troubleshoot a pipeline that works locally but fails in a remote environment due to a missing dependency, path issue, or network restriction.
assessment_rubric.socratic_prompt: Why do even simple data pipelines depend on Linux, networking, and version control practices in real production systems?
key_evaluation_criteria: Demonstrates practical systems literacy
Knows command-line and environment basics
Understands that data systems depend on operational reliability
assessment_rubric.remediation_hint: Practice diagnosing environment differences, not just writing code, because pipeline failures are often caused by infrastructure assumptions.

nodes.name: SQL, Relational Design, and Transactional Databases
core_concepts: MySQL, PostgreSQL, Aurora, SQL Server, Oracle

assessment_rubric.diagnostic_question: Describe how you would design a relational schema for customer orders, payments, and inventory while ensuring correctness under concurrent writes and query performance at scale.
assessment_rubric.socratic_prompt: Why do normalized designs and transactional guarantees differ from the needs of analytical reporting, and how do those trade-offs change across workloads?
key_evaluation_criteria: Understands relational modeling and data integrity
Can reason about query performance and indexing
Distinguishes OLTP and OLAP patterns clearly
assessment_rubric.remediation_hint: Design the entities and their constraints first, then optimize access patterns with indexes and materialized summaries only where the workload requires it.

nodes.name: NoSQL Data Stores and Alternative Data Models
core_concepts: Document, key-value, columnar, and graph databases
MongoDB, Cassandra, Redis, Neo4j, DynamoDB, Elasticsearch
When to use NoSQL instead of SQL
SCD patterns, star and snowflake schemas

assessment_rubric.diagnostic_question: A product team needs high-write throughput for user activity logs, flexible schema evolution, and fast lookups by session. Which storage pattern and database type fit best, and why?
assessment_rubric.socratic_prompt: Why can a system with incredibly fast reads still fail if the data model does not match the query pattern and the workload violates consistency assumptions?
key_evaluation_criteria: Matches database type to workload characteristics
Understands consistency and availability trade-offs
Chooses data modeling patterns appropriately
assessment_rubric.remediation_hint: Start by mapping the read and write patterns to a storage model before selecting a database product, because the data model drives both cost and correctness.

nodes.name: Data Warehouses, Data Lakes, and Lakehouse Concepts
core_concepts: Data lake, lakehouse, data mesh, and data fabric
BigQuery, Redshift, Snowflake, Databricks, Delta Lake

assessment_rubric.diagnostic_question: Explain when a company should choose a warehouse, a lake, or a lakehouse and how those choices affect cost, governance, and analytics performance.
assessment_rubric.socratic_prompt: Why do analytical systems often separate storage from compute, and how does that architectural decision influence speed, cost, and flexibility?
key_evaluation_criteria: Understands data modeling and warehouse/lakehouse trade-offs
Knows key cloud analytics architectures
Links storage choice to business and operational needs
assessment_rubric.remediation_hint: Model the workload first: how large, how structured, how often queried, and under what governance constraints before selecting the storage platform.

nodes.name: Data Ingestion, ETL, and Pipeline Design
core_concepts: Data extraction from databases, APIs, apps, and logs

assessment_rubric.diagnostic_question: Design a data ingestion pipeline that collects transactions from a payment system, normalizes them, and lands them in a warehouse while handling retries, partial failures, and schema drift safely.
assessment_rubric.socratic_prompt: Why is a pipeline that never fails silently still not useful if it produces low-quality, unvalidated data?
key_evaluation_criteria: Defines ingestion and transformation flow clearly
Handles failure, retry, and data quality concerns
Chooses ETL or ELT based on workload and governance needs
assessment_rubric.remediation_hint: Design the pipeline around the operational contract: what is expected to be delivered, how to detect bad data, and what the retry semantics should be under partial system failures.

nodes.name: Big Data, Cluster Computing, and Apache Spark
core_concepts: Distributed file systems and cluster management
HDFS, MapReduce, YARN, and job scheduling
Parallel processing and resilient data flows

assessment_rubric.diagnostic_question: When a daily ETL job that used to process a few million rows starts struggling with tens of billions of events, explain how you would redesign the job using cluster computing and distributed processing principles.
assessment_rubric.socratic_prompt: Why do distributed systems not just scale by raw power, and what additional concerns emerge around partitioning, scheduling, and failure handling?
key_evaluation_criteria: Understands cluster computing and distributed execution
Can reason about scaling and job orchestration
Connects architecture to throughput and resilience requirements
assessment_rubric.remediation_hint: Break the problem into partitionable work units, profile bottlenecks, and then design for sharding, retries, and efficient job scheduling rather than just adding more memory.

nodes.name: Streaming Data and Messaging Systems
core_concepts: Streaming data, event-driven systems, async communication

assessment_rubric.diagnostic_question: Design a streaming ingestion architecture that must process click events in near real time while maintaining order for an account and tolerating broker outages without data loss.
assessment_rubric.socratic_prompt: Why do asynchronous event systems require explicit handling of retries, ordering, and exactly-once semantics, and how do those choices affect correctness and cost?
key_evaluation_criteria: Understands messaging and event semantics
Handles failure and ordering realistically
Can reason about operational constraints of streaming systems
assessment_rubric.remediation_hint: Think through the semantics of delivery, durability, and consumer behavior before choosing a broker and partitioning pattern.

assessment_rubric.diagnostic_question: Explain how you would deploy a data pipeline to the cloud with secure credentials, scalable compute, and repeatable infrastructure provisioning using container and IaC principles.
assessment_rubric.socratic_prompt: Why do robust cloud deployments depend on immutability, environment separation, and declarative configuration rather than ad hoc manual changes?
key_evaluation_criteria: Understands cloud-native architecture and IaC
Can reason about scalability and environment management
Connects deployment design to secure and repeatable operations
assessment_rubric.remediation_hint: Treat infrastructure as code and environment configuration as first-class software, because repeatability is a core reliability feature in data systems.

nodes.name: Data Security, Governance, and Quality
core_concepts: Data lineage, governance, and metadata management

assessment_rubric.diagnostic_question: A healthcare data platform contains sensitive records and multiple consuming teams. Explain how you would protect the data while ensuring governance, lineage, and compliant access across the pipeline.
assessment_rubric.socratic_prompt: Why is governance not just a compliance issue but also a data quality and trust issue for downstream analytics and AI systems?
key_evaluation_criteria: Understands security and privacy controls
Can explain governance, lineage, and stewardship
Connects trust and compliance to operational data quality
assessment_rubric.remediation_hint: Make trust part of the data product contract: define who can access what, how it is protected, and how lineage and quality are maintained over time.

nodes.name: CI/CD, Observability, and Testing for Data Pipelines
core_concepts: Unit, integration, e2e, smoke, A/B, and load testing

assessment_rubric.diagnostic_question: Explain how you would design a deployment and monitoring strategy for a data pipeline that must run reliably in production and be recoverable when a transformation fails mid-run.
assessment_rubric.socratic_prompt: Why are smoke tests and runtime monitoring important in data engineering even when the code compiles successfully?
key_evaluation_criteria: Understands operational quality and deployment safety
Can design meaningful tests and monitoring
Links observability to reliability decisions
assessment_rubric.remediation_hint: Keep a close feedback loop between code changes, pipeline metrics, and operational incidents; reliability is built through repeated verification and transparent signals.

nodes.name: Data Serving, BI, Reverse ETL, and Productization
core_concepts: BI tools like Tableau, Power BI, Streamlit, Looker
Serving trusted data products to business users
Data as an internal platform capability

assessment_rubric.diagnostic_question: Describe how to deliver clean, trusted data to business users through dashboards, reverse ETL, and operational workflows without creating duplicate sources of truth.
assessment_rubric.socratic_prompt: Why do the most valuable data products align technology with business decisions, not just with storage or compute efficiency?
key_evaluation_criteria: Understands downstream consumption and business value
Can define productized data supply to stakeholders
Links technical reliability with business trust and usability
assessment_rubric.remediation_hint: Treat data as a product: define the user, contract, quality checks, and delivery path before expanding the platform.
